title: The lost galaxy
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 4535, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 4535 · constellation Virgo · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: NGC 4535 looks almost circular because we see it nearly face-on, set against a background of many faint, distant galaxies. A well-defined bar crosses its center, and its dust lanes bend sharply before the spiral arms split off from the ends of the bar. The arms are bluish, a sign of many hot young stars, while older, cooler stars give the central bulge a yellower tint.
The galaxy lies in the constellation Virgo and belongs to the Virgo Cluster, a huge gathering of up to 2000 galaxies about 50 million light-years away. It is one of the cluster's largest members.

Smaller amateur telescopes can pick it up, and William Herschel first observed it in 1785. Through such telescopes it looks hazy and ghostly, so the amateur astronomer Leland S. Copeland named it the Lost Galaxy in the 1950s.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.83 x 6.83 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 109,000 × 109,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS1 on the 8.2-meter Very Large Telescope observed NGC 4535 in visible light through B and V filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Through a small telescope the galaxy looks hazy and ghostly, while the VLT's exposures bring out its bar, dust lanes and colored arms.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The Virgo Cluster is not much wider than the Local Group, the group that includes the Milky Way, but it holds almost fifty times as many galaxies. This visible-light image came from the FORS1 instrument on ESO's 8.2-meter Very Large Telescope.
alt: A nearly circular barred spiral galaxy with bluish arms and a yellowish center, surrounded by small, faint background galaxies.
